name: comb
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The comb is a symbolic object. It links to the mermaid, who sat on a rock and combed her long hair to draw sailors toward death. By the rule of sympathetic magic, Scottish girls took care not to comb their hair at dusk while their brothers were at sea. The act could pull a dangerous mermaid toward their ship. Combing hair on a Wednesday brought sterility, though the cause stays unknown. In Ireland the comb held a firm tie to the goddess-queen Medb. It stood for the feminine force, above all in its evil form. Scottish lore held that wicked girls combed fleas and frogs from their locks, while good girls pulled out gold and jewels.

okr.objective: The comb is a Celtic symbol of feminine force and the mermaid.
